text:
support-ryan: raising an urgent customer escalation. tenant 98765 reporting KMS decrypt fails after a scheduled key rotation this morning. getting HTTP 403 from our proxy when trying to decrypt embeddings store. ticket: https://intercom.example/12345
security-jen: can you paste the exact error from logs? 403 usually means AccessDenied on KMS or encryption-context mismatch.
support-ryan: logs below from the repo service: 
```
2026-03-17T10:12:03Z ERROR decrypt failed status=403 kms=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef-1234 error=AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt
```
request payload includes encryption context: {project: redwood-prod, tenant: 98765}
maya-cs: customer says they didn't change anything on their side. They only saw a scheduled rotation note in our admin console at 09:58.
alex-plat: rotation job ran in us-west-2 at 09:58 and created new key version + disabled previous alias. I see a Canary run that should have validated decrypts but looks like it skipped for customers using cross-account KMS grants.
sre-luis: hypothesis: we rotated key (re-created CMK in our account) but didn't replicate or re-grant cross-account decrypt permission to the customer's account or to our worker role that assumes a cross-account role. Need to check grant+key policy.
security-jen: can you run quick check: aws kms list-grants --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef-1234 and also get-key-policy for the alias used? If the grant principal is missing for the service role, decrypts will 403.
support-ryan: ran list-grants, output truncated: 
```
Grants: [
  {GrantId: "g-1", GranteePrincipal: "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-worker", Operations: ["Decrypt"]}
]
```
get-key-policy returned a policy that only allows principals in account 111122223333 (our account) not the customer's account.
security-jen: that explains it for cross-account encrypted blobs. But customer 98765 is multi-tenant in our VPC; they expect us to retain access. Did the rotation replace the underlying key material without attaching previous grants?
alex-plat: rotation flow: create new key, attach alias, copy grants from old key -> attach. There's a race where we create key with default policy then attach grants; can cause decrypts during short window to fail. We should have used schedule with pre-warm step: create new key, attach grants, test decryption, then flip alias. Looks like our canary didn't run for accounts where encryption-context includes tenant.
sre-luis: repro steps I used locally: 
1) simulate encrypt with old key, encryption-context project=redwood-prod, tenant=98765
2) rotate: create new key, attach alias, but do NOT add grant for redwood-worker principal
3) attempt decrypt -> AccessDeniedException

Command I ran: 
```
aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin \
  --encryption-context project=redwood-prod,tenant=98765 \
  --key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef-1234
```
support-ryan: customer also included a copy of their audit logs showing repeated Decrypt errors 09:59-10:05. They included the ciphertext blob but we won't paste it here.
maya-cs: customer is asking for ETA to restore access and whether data was lost. We need a fast rollback or regrant.
security-jen: action plan: (1) escalate to infra to attach missing grants to the new key for redwood-worker and any cross-account principals for affected tenants, (2) run targeted replay to decrypt archived blobs for tenant 98765 to confirm no data loss, (3) add guard in rotation job to attach grants before alias flip and include encryption-context-aware canary.
ops-bot: incident created INC-2026-789, assigned to eng-runtime and eng-security, priority=P0.
alex-plat: I'm attaching a temporary mitigation script to attach grants at scale. Will run against keys created in last 24h with missing grants for known principals. Script (dry-run): 
```
for key in $(aws kms list-keys --region us-west-2 --query 'Keys[].KeyId' --output text); do
  grants=$(aws kms list-grants --key-id $key --query 'Grants[].GranteePrincipal' --output text)
  if ! echo "$grants" | grep -q "arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-worker"; then
    echo "attaching grant to $key"
    aws kms create-grant --key-id $key --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::444455556666:role/redwood-worker --operations Decrypt
  fi
done
```
security-jen: before you run, ensure kms:CreateGrant is permitted on the role you're using and that grants don't violate key policy. Also record grant ids for later revocation. Keep audit logs.
sre-luis: I'll coordinate a targeted replay to re-decrypt and re-encrypt blobs for tenant 98765 if needed. Requesting a short maintenance window 10:30-11:00.
maya-cs: customer agreed to maintenance window and wants a runbook update. They emphasized they need audit logs showing we re-granted and decrypted/re-encrypted as proof.
support-ryan: filed follow-up in ticket with mitigation steps and ETA. I'll post final once rotation job is patched. :thumbsup:
security-jen: follow-up tasks: (a) patch rotation orchestration to attach grants before alias switch, (b) add encryption-context canary to tests, (c) add automated policy check that copies key policy principals. I'll create GH issues.
alex-plat: good. I'll also add metric alerts for spike in kms:Decrypt AccessDenied per region.
support-ryan: thanks all, marking this thread monitored.
